extracted.intended_audience: trademark applicants and their attorneys filing ex parte appeals to the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formatting rules for taking an ex parte appeal to the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board, including notices of appeal, fees, multiple-class handling, and preparation/filing of appeal briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for Appeal / Appeal eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal to the Board may be taken from any final action, second refusal on the same ground(s), or repeated requirement issued by the examining attorney during the ex parte prosecution of an application for registration, except that a formal requirement which was the subject of a petition decided by the Director may not thereafter be the subject of an appeal to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal must be filed within six months from the date of the action from which the appeal is taken. If a notice of appeal is timely filed but the appeal fee is not, the appeal will be untimely and the application will be deemed abandoned. Filing a request for reconsideration does not stay the six-month appeal period. See TBMP § 1201.01, TBMP § 1201.05, and 37 CFR § 2.142(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal: form, content, and permissible filing methods
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal is the document by which an applicant appeals from the decision of the examining attorney refusing registration. The notice of appeal need consist only of a simple statement indicating that the applicant appeals from the refusal of registration; reasons for appeal need not be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing methods: strongly recommended through ESTTA (http://estta.uspto.gov); may also be filed by United States Mail or by facsimile transmission. The paper notice should bear the heading 'IN THE UNITED STATES PATENT AND TRADEMARK OFFICE BEFORE THE TRADEMARK TRIAL AND APPEAL BOARD' and identify the applicant, serial number, filing date, and mark. If the application has multiple classes and the appeal is not for all classes, indicate which class(es) are appealed. Only one copy should be submitted. The notice need not be verified and may be signed by the applicant, its attorney, or other authorized representative; an electronic signature will be accepted. The Board will accept a notice signed by an attorney who is not the attorney of record. An unsigned notice will not be refused consideration if a signed copy is submitted within the defect-correction time set by the Board. If the applicant believes the final action is premature, it should advise the Board (and can follow up via ESTTA). Do not combine the request for reconsideration or amendment in the body of the notice of appeal; indicate separately or check the ESTTA box if one is filed contemporaneously. See TBMP § 106.03, TBMP § 106.02, and TBMP § 1204.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Fee: payment per class and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must pay the prescribed appeal fee for each class in the application for which an appeal is taken, within six months of the date of issuance of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no appeal fee is paid for at least one class before the six-month statutory period expires, the application will be abandoned. In multiple-class applications, fees must be paid for each appealed class; if fees are submitted for fewer than all classes and the applicant has not specified classes, the Board will notify the applicant to pay additional fees or specify classes; otherwise the Board will apply fees to classes in ascending order (lowest numbered first). If a timely notice of appeal is filed but the appeal fee is not, the appeal will be untimely and the applicant may file a petition to revive in some circumstances. Deposit-account general authorizations to charge fees will be accepted if funds are sufficient. Fee amount and specifics are in 37 CFR § 2.6(a)(18) and 37 CFR § 2.141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-class applications and requests to divide
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application contains multiple classes and the final refusal/requirement pertains to some but not all classes, the applicant may (a) file an appeal for the application as a whole, or (b) file a request to divide the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant appeals only some classes, classes not appealed that have final refusals/requirements will be deemed abandoned (unless a timely request for reconsideration is pending and later remanded). If a request to divide is filed with a notice of appeal, the appeal will be suspended until action on the request to divide. Classes or goods/services that have been divided out and for which no final refusal/requirement has issued will proceed to publication or registration and will not be delayed pending the appeal. If the final refusal/requirement does not pertain to all classes, appeal fees are required only for classes appealed. See TBMP § 1205.02 and 37 CFR § 2.87.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and physical format requirements for briefs and paper submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper submissions must meet formatting requirements: printed in at least 11-point type, double-spaced, text on one side only, paper dimensions 8 to 8.5 by 11 to 11.69 inches, no tabs or extruding devices, dividers without extruding tabs, not stapled or bound, all pages numbered, and exhibits identified as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions may be made electronically where permitted; electronic text must be at least 11-point and double-spaced; exhibits for electronic submissions must be attached electronically. Exhibits pertaining to a paper submission must be filed on paper and comply with paper submission requirements. These requirements derive from 37 CFR § 2.126 and govern briefs under 37 CFR § 2.142(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief content requirements and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief must be in written form, meet § 2.126 requirements, and contain an alphabetical index of cited cases. The case citation should include a USPQ citation if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without prior leave, a brief shall not exceed 25 pages in its entirety, including table of contents, index of cases, description of the record, statement of the issues, recitation of the facts, argument, and summary. The brief need not include formal trial-brief requirements (but if included they count toward the page limit). The brief should indicate it is an appeal brief and identify the application (applicant's name, serial number, filing date, and mark). The brief should not include a proposed amendment, request for remand, or request for oral hearing within its body — those must be filed as separately captioned papers. Appendices or exhibits may not be used to avoid the page limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limit enforcement and anti-circumvention
rubrics_metrics.description: The 25-page limit for an appeal brief is strictly enforced; briefs exceeding the limit without prior leave will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although an overlength brief will not be treated as failure to file a brief (and thus not automatically dismiss the appeal), the Board will not consider the nonconforming brief; the examining attorney may still file a brief and the applicant may file a reply limited to responding to the examining attorney’s arguments. The Board has sanctioned attempts to circumvent page limits (e.g., submitting discussion in an appendix) and will rarely grant leave to exceed the limit. Parties are encouraged to highlight the most probative evidence rather than submitting voluminous exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and exhibits: what to submit and what to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Material that was not previously made of record should not be submitted with the appeal brief. Appendices/exhibits to a brief do not count toward the page limit but may not be used to circumvent it. Materials already in the application file should not routinely be resubmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If large amounts of evidence were submitted during prosecution, parties are encouraged to identify the most probative pieces by date and page number so the Board can easily locate them. The Board disfavors submitting hundreds of pages of third-party registrations or other evidence without highlighting relevant items. Exhibits to paper submissions must comply with paper-format rules; exhibits for electronic submissions must be attached electronically. See TBMP § 1203.01 and related case law (e.g., In re Lorillard Licensing Co., In re Max Capital Group Ltd.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing the applicant's main brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant's main brief must be filed within 60 days from the date of appeal (or within an extension of time for that purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the brief is not filed within the time allowed, the appeal may be dismissed. If a brief is filed late, the applicant may submit an explanation; acceptance depends on circumstances including the length of delay. If the appeal is dismissed for failure to file a timely brief, the applicant may petition the Director under 37 CFR § 2.146(a)(3) only after first filing a request/motion to accept the late-filed brief and being denied. A petition to revive under 37 CFR § 2.66(a) is not available for late or omitted briefs because filing an appeal brief is not a response to an Office action. Certificate-of-mailing rules: date of mailing is used for timeliness of notice of appeal, but actual date of receipt used for running of time for filing main brief. If a request for reconsideration is pending and proceedings are suspended/remanded, do not file the appeal brief within 60 days as originally set; the Board will resume and set briefing time after remand outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and rules for the examining attorney's brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after the Board's written action forwarding the application to the examining attorney (or within an extension), the examining attorney must file an appeal brief answering the applicant's main brief and mail a copy to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examining attorney's brief is late-filed, the Board may exclude it absent adequate explanation. An examining attorney’s failure to file a brief will not result in approval; the Board will decide the appeal without the benefit of the brief. If persuaded by the applicant's brief that registration is appropriate, the examining attorney may approve the application for publication or registration and should notify the applicant. If the examining attorney withdraws a ground, the brief should state that withdrawal — but omission of a ground in the brief may be treated as a withdrawal by the Board. See TBMP § 1203.02(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing channels, ESTTA advantages, and prohibited media
rubrics_metrics.description: ESTTA filing is strongly encouraged for notices of appeal and briefs; it provides immediate confirmation, an electronically generated order instituting the appeal, and the date by which the appeal brief is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of appeal is the only paper that may be filed by facsimile transmission with the Board. The Board's rules have been amended such that briefs may no longer be filed on CD-ROM. For more information about ESTTA filing procedures and parameters see TBMP § 106.03 and TBMP § 110.09 and 37 CFR § 2.126(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and representation rules for filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal must be signed but need not be verified; it may be signed by the applicant or its attorney or other authorized representative; an electronic signature will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will accept a notice signed by an attorney even if that attorney is not the attorney of record; the Board will continue to correspond only with the attorney of record or the applicant if no attorney is appointed. However, the Trademark Examining Operation will not accept any document (including a request for reconsideration filed with a notice of appeal) if signed by an applicant or an attorney when a different attorney had been appointed to act and the power has not been revoked. Unsigned notices may be cured if a signed copy is submitted within the time set by the Board for correction. See TBMP § 106.02 and related notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of requests for reconsideration with appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may file a request for reconsideration (with or without amendment/new evidence) during the period between issuance of a final action and the expiration of time for filing an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a request for reconsideration does not stay the six-month time for filing an appeal. If the applicant files a timely notice of appeal and a request for reconsideration is pending or filed contemporaneously, the Board will institute the appeal, suspend proceedings, and remand the application to the examining attorney for consideration of the request. Proceedings in the appeal are automatically suspended while reconsideration is pending, and applicant should not file its appeal brief within the usual 60-day period while suspension/remand is in effect. If the examining attorney is not persuaded and issues a non-final Office action or a new final refusal, the classes not appealed may be deemed abandoned unless further action is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of late appeals, insufficient fees, and available remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of appeal is timely filed but the appeal fee is not, the appeal will be untimely and the application will be deemed abandoned; however, an applicant may sometimes petition to revive. If an appeal is late-filed but the applicant timely filed some other response (e.g., amendment or request for reconsideration), the Board will notify the applicant that the appeal cannot be entertained and will forward the application to the examining attorney for appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may petition the Director to revive an application for failure to file a timely appeal (since an appeal is considered a response to an Office action), but the 'unintentional delay' standard of 37 CFR § 2.66(a) does not apply to applications abandoned due to an incomplete response after a final Office action. A request for reconsideration that is not accompanied by a notice of appeal is an incomplete response; if such a request is denied, the Director's practice is to deny a petition to revive in such circumstances. For late-filed briefs, a petition to revive is not available because briefing is not an Office-action response; instead the applicant should first move to accept the late-filed brief and, if denied, may petition the Director under supervisory authority (37 CFR § 2.146(a)(3)).
